abstract: Lenoir et al. (https://doi.org/10.1083/jcb.202601063) find that MapZ phosphorylation by the serine/threonine protein kinase StkP modulates interactions with EzrA, regulating septum dynamics in Streptococcus pneumoniae. Phosphorylation control ensures proper spatial-temporal control of cell division, emphasizing the role of serine threonine protein kinases (STKP) in these bacteria.
